ai.description: *Hemidactylus persicus* reaches 60 mm SVL. It is pale grey to yellowish with dark dorsal crossbands. Key features include strongly keeled ventral scales and a tail covered in rows of pointed tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus persicus* is best distinguished by its strongly keeled, trihedral dorsal tubercles and the presence of a distinct, dark longitudinal stripe through the eye.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus persicus* inhabits arid to semi-arid rocky outcrops and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Persian gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively hunt insects and spiders along rock faces and human structures.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus persicus* is oviparous, laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus persicus* occurs in the arid regions of northwestern India, specifically within the states of Rajasthan and Gujarat, typically at low elevations.
